main_text.p: bat extensa & distenta illa intestini duodeni portio. Quin etiam dubitare nemo poterat quid esset πομαυξησις sive mole augeri: uti & quid sit ζήσις, ὀγκωσις, πνεύματωσις καὶ αὔξησις, quibus σφύξιν definit Arist. lib. de resp. cap. 20. & 21. rarefacti enim illi humores, & flatibus bullisve effervescentiâ excitatis admodum distenti, non potuerunt non majorem locum occupare. Parvâ enim humorum copiâ effluente intestinū longè reddebatur flaccidius propter discessum subtilioris materiæ sive flatuum, vel si mavis halituosi spiritûs, interstitia distractorū humorum occupantium. Non ingratū erat intelligere quare subtilior illa materia, quæ per poros intestini illius ingressa fuerat, ex illo pari facilitate non effluat; sed ibidem permaneat: distractis videlicet humorum illorum partibus, intestino illo motu sive effervescentiâ, non possunt non illorum interstitia, quandoquidem omnia plena sunt, materiâ

page.notes: Greek words in the text are transcribed as closely as the scan allows; the first Greek word (πομαυξησις-like, printed "πο͂ιλα-σις" with a ligature) and the Greek after "ζήσις" are partly uncertain. Catchword "materiâ" is printed at the right foot. The printed word "Quin" and "effluat" are as printed. A dark ink mark over "resp." is a stain.
